a4124.speech: “It's certainly been years, perhaps decades, since the Senate has passed a bill that so greatly impacts not just our national security, not just the security of our allies, but the security of Western democracy” ; told a news conference he was confident the bill would pass the House with support from both parties if Republican Speaker Mike Johnson would allow a vote: “I call on Speaker Johnson to rise to the occasion, to do the right thing: Bring this bill to the floor quickly.”

a4124.speaker: Mike Johnson, US House Speaker (statement)
a4124.speech: Issued a statement before the Senate vote faulting it for lacking conservative provisions to stem a record flow of migrants across the US-Mexico border, suggesting he would not schedule a vote any time soon: “In the absence of having received any single border policy change from the Senate, the House will have to continue to work its own will on these important matters” ; “America deserves better than the Senate's status quo.”

a4124.speaker: Joe Biden, US President (statement)
a4124.speech: Issued a statement urging the House to move swiftly: “If we do not stand against tyrants who seek to conquer or carve up their neighbors' territory, the consequences for America's national security will be significant” ; “Our allies and adversaries alike will take note.”

a4124.speaker: Ukrainian officials
a4124.speech: Have warned of weapons shortages at a time when Russia is pressing ahead with renewed attacks.

a4124.speaker: Volodymyr Zelenskiy, Ukrainian President (post on X)
a4124.speech: Quickly hailed passage of the bill: “American assistance brings just peace in Ukraine closer and restores global stability, resulting in increased security and prosperity for all Americans and all the free world.”

a4124.speaker: Donald Trump, frontrunner for the Republican presidential nomination (social media)
a4124.speech: Has criticized the aid package on social media, saying it should take the form of a loan, and also worried US allies by suggesting he could encourage aggression against some NATO members.

a4124.speaker: John Thune, No. 2 Senate Republican
a4124.speech: Said it was not clear what Johnson would do: “The House, I assume, is going to move on something. Obviously, they're going to address Israel.”

a4124.speaker: Rick Scott, Republican Senator of Florida
a4124.speech: Said in an early morning floor speech: “The bill before us today ... will never pass in the House, will never become law.”

a4124.speaker: Hardline Republicans
a4124.speech: Predicted the Senate legislation would be dead on arrival in the House.

a4222.speaker: Dr Amadou Hamadoun Dicko, lecturer-researcher in microbial biotechnology, University of Segou (patron of the graduating class)
a4222.speech: Said he was very moved by his students’ decision to associate his name with the class: “I want to express to them all my gratitude for this consideration. It means that I must redouble my efforts in my mission of training the country’s future senior staff.”

a4222.speaker: Dr Amadou Hamadoun Dicko, patron of the graduating class (advice to graduates)
a4222.speech: Urged the new graduates to pursue their efforts in order to meet the professional challenges that await them: “I advised them to work tirelessly in order to serve their country with honour and dedication, and to improve themselves so as to be competitive on the national and international market.”

a4280.speaker: Barchue Toure, newly trained Process Operator, ArcelorMittal Liberia Training Academy beneficiary
a4280.speech: Described his training experience at the ArcelorMittal Liberia Training Academy as nothing short of transformational, and reflected on his initial uncertainties and how they were gradually replaced by confidence and competence: "When I first started, I was filled with excitement and enthusiasm, but also a bit of uncertainty," he admitted. "I had never worked in a mine before. As we embarked on this journey, it was eye-opening—it expanded my knowledge beyond what I ever imagined." ; "This training was not just about learning—it was about growing. We are not just going to move iron, we are going to move history," Toure emphasized. "Some people think we're just here to participate, to blend in. But we didn't come here to participate—we came to define the future of iron ore mining in West Africa."

a4280.speaker: Barchue Toure, newly trained Process Operator, ArcelorMittal Liberia Training Academy beneficiary
a4280.speech: Commended ArcelorMittal Liberia's commitment not only to technical excellence but also to Liberia's broader national development, saying the company's massive investment in local talent development and infrastructure is changing lives and charting a new direction for Liberia's economy: "What we're doing here is far beyond image or profit. ArcelorMittal is investing in Liberia's future. This Iron Ore Processing Plant is more than a structure—it's a symbol of transformation, opportunity, and progress."

a4280.speaker: Barchue Toure, newly trained Process Operator, ArcelorMittal Liberia Training Academy beneficiary
a4280.speech: Stressed the deeper, more personal impact of the training program: "Being part of this transformation is an honor," he said. "It means my work will help shape a better Liberia. It means I have the tools to change my life and support my community. That's the kind of impact that lasts."

a4700.speaker: André Snyman, Managing Director of Walvis Bay Salt
a4700.speech: Welcomed this development, but pointed to challenges such as high import duties and non-tariff barriers to trade, and noted the irony of “free” trade under such conditions.

a4700.speaker: Selma Ashipala-Musavyi, Namibian Trade Minister
a4700.speech: Stressed the need to involve the private sector and announced a national initiative to remove trade barriers.

a4700.speaker: Officials (unnamed)
a4700.speech: Also called for an accelerated implementation of the AfCFTA in order to boost intra-African trade.

a5063.speaker: Donald Trump, US President
a5063.speech: Posted on Truth Social that he had called Putin to begin arranging talks between the Russian leader and Zelensky ; said that following such a bilateral, at a location to be determined, there would be a trilateral where the US president would join them.

a5063.speaker: Putin adviser (unnamed)
a5063.speech: Said afterwards that Trump and Putin spoke for 40 minutes by phone on Monday.

a5063.speaker: Donald Trump, US President (hot-mic remarks to French President Emmanuel Macron)
a5063.speech: “I think he wants to make a deal. I think he wants to make a deal for me. You understand that? As crazy as that sounds,” Trump told Macron, appearing to refer to Putin.

a5063.speaker: Yuri Ushakov, Kremlin aide
a5063.speech: A noncommittal statement on Monday night said it was “worthwhile” to “explore the possibility of raising the level of representatives” from the Russian and Ukrainian delegations in negotiations.

a5063.speaker: Donald Trump, US President
a5063.speech: Seemed to dismiss the need for any ceasefire before negotiations to end the war can take place: “I don't know that it's necessary,” Trump said of a ceasefire.

a5063.speaker: Friedrich Merz, German Chancellor
a5063.speech: “I can't imagine that the next meeting would take place without a ceasefire. So, let's work on that and let's try to put pressure on Russia.”

a5063.speaker: Donald Trump, US President
a5063.speech: Told Zelensky the US would help guarantee Ukraine's security in any deal to end the war, without specifying the extent of any assistance; when asked by reporters whether US security guarantees for Ukraine could include any American military in the country, Trump did not rule it out; he said Europe was the “first line of defence”, but that “we'll be involved” ; “We'll give them good protection” ; he also said that during last week's Alaska summit Putin had accepted that there would be security guarantees for Ukraine as part of any peace deal.

a5063.speaker: Volodymyr Zelensky, President of Ukraine
a5063.speech: Said at a news conference after Monday's meetings that part of the security guarantee would involve a $90bn (£67bn) arms deal between the US and Ukraine; said this would include US weapons that Ukraine does not have, including aviation systems, anti-missile systems “and other things I will not disclose”; also said the US would buy Ukrainian drones, which would help fund their domestic production of the unmanned craft ; told reporters that security guarantees for Kyiv would probably be worked out within 10 days.

a5063.speaker: Volodymyr Zelensky, President of Ukraine
a5063.speech: Handing his host a letter from Ukrainian First Lady Olena Zelenska to be delivered to US First Lady Melania Trump: “It's not to you – [it's] to your wife,” he told Trump.

a5063.speaker: Mark Rutte, Nato chief
a5063.speech: “I really want to thank you for your leadership.”

a5063.speaker: Giorgia Meloni, Italian Prime Minister
a5063.speech: Said while there had previously been no sign that Russia wanted to move towards peace “something had changed” thanks to Trump.

a5063.speaker: Emmanuel Macron, French President
a5063.speech: Told fellow leaders somberly: “When we talk about security guarantees, we're also talking about the matter of the security of the European continent.”

a5078.speaker: Nana Yaw Barimah Barnie, Regional Communication Officer of Ghana Water Limited (GWL)
a5078.speech: Made known to the Daily Graphic last Tuesday that the indebted customers were largely private consumers, including companies, domestic customers, water sellers and operators of washing bays ; "The list of debtors does not include ministries, departments and agencies (MDAs) because the government has paid all bills for these institutions to the extent that many of their accounts are in credit." ; said the indebtedness by the private customers of the GWL had plunged the company into huge financial challenges, affecting the company's ability to meet the water demand and supply gap; explained that while millions of dollars was spent on importation of chemicals for the treatment of water, the failure by customers to fully pay had worsened the financial situation ; "We hope to recover that money by the end of this month (February); and so, we are cautioning all persons who are indebted to the company to take immediate steps to clear their outstanding balance before we take legal action against them."

a5078.speaker: Nana Yaw Barimah Barnie, Regional Communication Officer of Ghana Water Limited (GWL)
a5078.speech: Said the GWL team would also check illegal connections by some customers; said that despite struggling to produce water at exorbitant cost, some customers used unorthodox means of tapping water from GWL's service lines without paying for it; explained that some of those people used an in-line booster pump to suck water from the GWL service lines into their houses ; "This is wrong. The booster pump should be installed in such a way that it sucks water from underground tank into the overhead tank of customers instead of the tapping water from the service line of GWL."

a5078.speaker: Nana Yaw Barimah Barnie, Regional Communication Officer of Ghana Water Limited (GWL)
a5078.speech: Added that as part of measures to ensure effective revenue mobilisation, the company had introduced electronic payment of water bills; said that with the aid of a mobile application, customers could download the GWL app and use it to pay bills and access the statement of account; said the process had begun for GWL to go paperless in terms of the billing of customers ; "We have started piloting the electronic billing system at the Agbogba District and this will holistically be rolled out to cover the entire region."

a5350.speaker: Dr Rashid Mfaume, Director of Health, Social Welfare and Nutrition Services at the President's Office (Regional Administration and Local Government Authority)
a5350.speech: Said that currently about 85% of health care services in Dar es Salaam are provided by private health care facilities ; ‘The government has shown political will and implemented policies that create a conducive environment for private sector stakeholders to work towards achieving their goals while collaborating with the government’

a5350.speaker: Dr Denis Mzaga, Director of Strategic Information for USAID Afya Yangu Southern
a5350.speech: ‘USAID Afya Yangu is providing support to 752 Health Facilities (HFs) in 6 regions. Of the supported HFs, 145 (19.3%) are from private with 80,329 (27%) clients on ART which is more than any of the supported regions (Iringa is the largest with 65,468 clients)’

a5350.speaker: Kenneth Chima, Deputy Chief of Party for USAID Kizazi Hodari Southern Zone
a5350.speech: Said despite these achievements, the projects still faces challenges due to limited funding and competing from the government priorities.

a5350.speaker: Godfrey Nyombi, USAID Tanzania Head of System Strengthening
a5350.speech: Said that USAID works in supporting government health projects that touches lives of Tanzanians from grassroots level with an aim of improving lives. "USAID is very proud of this health forum which highlight the achievements of projects that we have been funding. We will continue working and collaborating with the Tanzania government for purpose of making lives of Tanzanians and especially those living in rural areas better."

a5384.speaker: A source (anonymous), cited by US gossip blog the Jasmine Brand
a5384.speech: told popular US gossip blog, the Jasmine Brand that he cheated on his girlfriend, Jhené Aiko ; “They were all over each other and they looked really comfortable around each other. They looked like they were a couple,” the source claimed.

a5384.speaker: InTouch Weekly
a5384.speech: According to InTouch Weekly, no cameras were allowed inside the party, so they thought nobody would see - but somebody reportedly spilled the cheating beans to Jhené.

a5384.speaker: Jhené Aiko, singer (Twitter post)
a5384.speech: took to Twitter to hit back at the rumours: “Sorry, but nothing about you guy's fan fiction stories are true... I still love you tho”.

a5384.speaker: The Shade Room
a5384.speech: According to The Shade Room, she later unfollowed Big Sean on Instagram.

a5384.speaker: Phetole Given Mogale (@GivVi_G), Twitter user
a5384.speech: “Now that we all know it's all lies, Big Sean is going to release a song confirming his love for Jhene Aiko and still find a way to squeeze in his grandma on the 3rd verse”

a5468.speaker: Senator (Dr) Barau I. Jibrin, Deputy President of the Senate
a5468.speech: Announced his plans to raise 558 young farmer millionaires this farming season; according to a statement from his media team, under a program tagged Barau Initiative for Agricultural Revolution in the North West (BIARN), three young farmers will be selected from each of the 186 local government areas of the seven states that comprise the North West geopolitical zone: Kano, Kaduna, Katsina, Kebbi, Jigawa, Sokoto and Zamfara, with each beneficiary receiving N5 million and a total of N2.79 billion disbursed ; addressing members of the Senate Press Corps at the National Assembly on Thursday, he said BIARN was established to boost the agricultural sector towards attaining food security in line with President Bola Ahmed Tinubu GCFR's Renewed Hope Agenda, and, speaking through his Special Adviser on Policy and Monitoring, Professor Bashir Muhammad Fagge, said the initiative is being coordinated by his foundation, the Barau I Jibrin Foundation (BIJF).

a5468.speaker: Senator (Dr) Barau I. Jibrin, Deputy President of the Senate (press conference statement, delivered by Special Adviser Professor Bashir Muhammad Fagge)
a5468.speech: "Ladies and gentlemen of the journalism profession and our partners in progress, good morning and welcome to this press conference organised by my foundation, the Barau I. Jibrin Foundation (BIJF), to inform the public about my initiative to revolutionise the agricultural sector of our country in line with the Renewed Hope Agenda of the President and Commander-In-Chief of the Armed Forces of the Federal Republic of Nigeria, His Excellency Bola Ahmed Tinubu, GCFR." ; "Food security is paramount and at the top of the agenda of progressive nations globally. Without it, you are insecure at the individual, family, local government, state, and country levels. If you recall, decades ago, the North, especially the North West, was our country's food basket, producing most of the agricultural products for consumption by the people nationwide and even for export to our neighbouring countries. However, that has become history. To change the narrative and harness the enormous arable land across the seven North West states, I have developed the initiative of empowering 558 young farmers in the North West geopolitical zone for the first phase of the programme." ; "My foundation, the Barau I Jibrin Foundation (BIJF), is partnering with a relevant national financial institution to implement this programme. It will interest you to know that we have had a series of meetings with the institution's management. Arrangements for the project's launch are almost complete. The initiative's targeted April this year to launch fully, ahead of this year's farming season... Each selected beneficiary will receive an interest-free N5 million loan to invest in farming during this year's cropping season. The sum of N2.79 billion will be disbursed to the beneficiaries. The breakdown of the beneficiaries per state is as follows: Kaduna 69, Kano 132, Kebbi 63, Katsina 102, Jigawa 81, Sokoto 69 and Zamfara 42."

a5718.speaker: #TakeItBackMovement (protest organisers)
a5718.speech: Had declared June 12 a "National Day of Resistance", rejecting what they called the "hollow ceremonies" of Democracy Day.

a5718.speaker: Wasiu Abiodun, spokesperson for the Niger State police command
a5718.speech: Said officers were deployed "for public safety but no protester was seen at the venue."

a5718.speaker: Residents of Kano State
a5718.speech: Told Daily Trust that they were not aware of the protest.

a5718.speaker: Aisha Ibrahim, food vendor at Kofar Naisa, Kano
a5718.speech: "This morning, I opened my shop like I always do. People are buying food, and nobody has said anything about any protest. I think many people in Kano are not even aware anything like that is happening."

a5718.speaker: Malam Ibrahim Musa, textile trader at Kwari Market, Kano
a5718.speech: Said politics is not on the minds of most people at the moment: "People are more concerned about survival. Things are expensive, and what we need now is customers, not protest. Maybe in Lagos or Abuja it's happening, but here, everybody is doing business as usual."

a5718.speaker: Hafiz Lawal, coordinator of the protest in Edo State
a5718.speech: Said it was shelved for security reasons.

a5718.speaker: Dungus Abdulkarim, spokesman of the Yobe State police command
a5718.speech: Told our correspondent that the command was not notified about the protest.

a5718.speaker: #Endbadgovernance Movement (placards)
a5718.speech: Displayed placards with inscriptions; "No one deserves death sentence for protesting against hunger", "we pay through our nose, Eko Disco smiles to the bank", and others, expressing their grievances over hardship exacerbated by the president's economic reforms.

a5718.speaker: Hassan Taiwo Soweto, a leader of the #Endbadgovernance movement
a5718.speech: "These are the people who should have been part of the pro-democracy struggle, but when you see what president Bola Tinubu is doing today over the past two years, you are going to realise that there is nothing democratic under his government. We are here today to demonstrate the fact that the democracy that the Nigerian people fought for in 1993 have been bastardised by President Bola Tinubu and the APC. Today, there is no freedom of speech. In fact, what we have today is a capitalist-dictatorship under the president. That is why we have to question the democratic credentials of the president."

a5718.speaker: Bestman Nze-Jumbo, leader of Team Nigeria (pro-Tinubu group)
a5718.speech: "We are celebrating. This is the first time that Nigeria will go over 20 years of democratic rule at a stretch and all this took effect from the spirit of June 12th. If you were around during June 12th, you will know that it is a day worth celebrating. You know, in Nigeria, people play to the gallery. They want to be seen as if they are on the side of those suffering. Well, it is not true. Every protest that you see is probably sponsored. Now, that is why I said what my group is doing is not a protest, it is a celebration. June 12 is worth celebrating in Nigeria, because it is about our democracy and MKO Abiola who eventually gave his life."

a5718.speaker: A coalition of civil socialists, labour activists and students in Oyo State
a5718.speech: Demonstrators calling on the federal and state governments to end "hunger, hardship, insecurity, reverse all International Monetary Fund/World Bank anti-poor policies and end attacks on democratic rights for genuine electoral reform."

a5718.speaker: Aremu, protest leader in Oyo State
a5718.speech: "We are out today because today is June 12. Unfortunately for us, there are hardly any dividends to show for it. What we have today is what they call renewed hope, which has ceased to be truly one. The government of President Bola Tinubu has been in office since May 29, 2025. For working people, youth and other ordinary Nigerians, the administration, whose mantra is 'Renewed Hope Agenda', has proved to be a monumental failure."

a5718.speaker: Abiodun Bamgboye, secretary of the Joint Action Front (JAF)
a5718.speech: Alleged that "Nigerians are suffering from "an outrageous spike in fuel price, inadequacy of electricity generation and distribution. We demand immediate repositioning of all public refineries and an end to the importation of petroleum products, nationalisation of the power sector under the control and management of the elected representatives of the working people. Our schools are not in the best conditions."

a5718.speaker: Residents of Osun State who protested in Osogbo
a5718.speech: Urged the federal government to address the economic hardship in the country.

a5718.speaker: Victor Lijofi, coordinator of the #TakeItBackMovement in Osun State
a5718.speech: Asked Tinubu to alleviate poverty in Nigeria.

a5799.speaker: William Butterfield, USAID representative in Angola
a5799.speech: Announced an investment of US$3.5 million to support the environmental issues of local organisations in the Lobito Corridor, at the opening of the Lobito Corridor Coordination Conference; emphasised the fundamental role of this infrastructure in regional integration, linking the African continent, expanding export opportunities and boosting trade. “We recognise that building infrastructure can generate environmental concerns. That’s why we will invest US$3.5 million to support local organisations in Angola, ensuring that the processes are fair and accountable,” William Butterfield said today, stressing that “USAID will also help improve the government’s auditing capabilities, minimising fraud and abuse”. ; Said the Lobito Corridor will create many job opportunities, strengthen local economies and improve the quality of life of the communities along its route. “The new Lobito Atlantic Railway is one of the most important transport infrastructure projects the United States has supported in Africa in a generation. It will strengthen regional trade and growth and advance our shared vision of creating an interconnected railway network from the Atlantic Ocean to the Indian Ocean,” he said. ; Stressed that one of the objectives of the Lobito Corridor is to relieve congestion on southern routes, such as Durban, South Africa, and Beira, Mozambique, by offering another transport alternative; said prioritising rail transport will reduce Africa’s carbon footprint, pointing out that recently the United States Development Finance Corporation approved up to US$533 million for the Lobito Corridor and the US Export-Import Bank “granted a historic loan of US$1.6 billion to support 65 solar energy mini-grids in four provinces of Angola”.

a5799.speaker: Ted Lawrence, deputy director of Power Africa
a5799.speech: Said that this initiative led by the US government and coordinated by USAID, has already helped to mobilise more than US$25 billion for electrification projects across sub-Saharan Africa, much of it from the private sector; said the Lobito Corridor offers an opportunity to tackle the energy deficit that has long hindered growth in sub-Saharan Africa, highlighting Power Africa’s vast experience in working with governments to strengthen energy policies, ‘creating the right regulatory environments to attract investment’, while also ensuring environmental preservation.

a5813.speaker: Sadiya Lawal, 21, former GGSS Jangebe student abducted in 2021
a5813.speech: “It was a few days after we resumed school,” she began, her gaze shifting away as memories of that night resurfaced.

a5813.speaker: Amsau Yusuf, former GGSS Jangebe student
a5813.speech: said she thought one of their teachers was trying to wake them for the Subh (morning) prayers; “Wake up now, or I'll kill you,” Ms Yusuf recalled one of the bandits shouting. “We were trying to hide, and they pointed guns at us. We started crying, and they herded us like cattle.”

a5813.speaker: Sadiya Lawal, former GGSS Jangebe student
a5813.speech: “A lot changed when we came back. Just the nature of schooling here is not the same. I prefer it there (GGSS Jangebe).” ; said dropping out and marrying in December 2022 was a choice she said felt okay at the time.

a5813.speaker: Fatima Musa, 18, former GGSS Jangebe student
a5813.speech: “When we wrote (WASSCE), there's no money to say I'll apply for admission or anything. That's why.”

a5813.speaker: SBM Intelligence (compiled data)
a5813.speech: According to data compiled by SBM Intelligence, since the first recorded mass abduction of 276 girls at Government Girls Secondary School, Chibok, Borno State, by Boko Haram terrorists in 2014, more than 1,700 students and teachers have been abducted in Northern Nigeria.

a5813.speaker: PREMIUM TIMES (previous reporting)
a5813.speech: reported last year how years of insecurity and mass abductions in the region have crippled basic education and led to the closure of over 60 primary and secondary schools.

a5813.speaker: United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organisation (UNESCO)
a5813.speech: According to UNESCO, Nigeria has over 20 million out-of-school children, with the 'degenerating security' situation in the region described as a major driver.

a5813.speaker: Aisha Nasir, 17, former GGSS Jangebe student
a5813.speech: “I resumed on Sunday, and the abduction happened on Thursday,” she recalled; on captivity: “They cook rice and beans. We fetch water, and they put our portion in a sack” ; said she didn't think about going back to school because she “started getting disinterested”, but after being forced to re-enroll at GGDSS Anka, “Gradually, I started getting interested again.”

a5813.speaker: Firdausi Sani, former GGSS Jangebe student
a5813.speech: “They told us it was fate, and it could've happened to anyone.”

a5813.speaker: Farida Lawali, former GGSS Jangebe student
a5813.speech: “It wasn't up to a month (after the release). My father wanted me to go to school so he took me there (GGSS Maru).”

a5813.speaker: Ruqayya Muhammad, mother of Farida Lawali
a5813.speech: “We were thrown into sadness during their abduction, but we finally admitted it as her fate as destined by God. We were excited when they got back safely. So, we decided that she would go back to school immediately” ; “Now that she's done with her NCE, we are happy that we gave her the foundation of education.”

a5813.speaker: Zainab Ibrahim, former GGSS Jangebe student
a5813.speech: “I want to study Nursing, but my father wants me to study Medical Laboratory Science. So, I started at Sarkin Zamfara College of Health.”

a5813.speaker: Nuradden Sulaiman, vice-principal of GGSS Jangebe
a5813.speech: told PREMIUM TIMES that since the conversion the school has seen less student population: “We used to have over 1000 students, but we currently have less than 500. We have 10 classes. But only nine are occupied.”

a5813.speaker: Nuradden Sulaiman, vice-principal of GGSS Jangebe
a5813.speech: said the computers were not used as often as necessary due to the lack of constant electricity: “We use them for practicals, and we have a generator, but due to the high cost of fueling it, we can't always afford to fuel it.”

a5813.speaker: Nuradden Sulaiman, vice-principal of GGSS Jangebe
a5813.speech: According to the vice-principal, the security situation in the community has improved since the abduction; he has many expectations for the school's operations: “If possible, the boarding system should resume.”

a5813.speaker: Staff and students of GGSS Jangebe
a5813.speech: say they believe the security situation in the community has improved.

a5848.speaker: Nigerian man deported from the US to Ghana (anonymous)
a5848.speech: Told the BBC he is now stuck in a hotel in Togo after he and five others were secretly transferred there by Ghanaian officers, who he alleged took them through a back route after bribing local police and without informing Togolese authorities: "They did not take us through the main border, they took us through the back door. They paid the police there and dropped us in Togo." ; said officials had told them at the camp they were being taken to a hotel for more comfort: "When we arrived, we asked what we were doing at the border, and they told us they wanted us to sign some paperwork so they could take us to a hotel, but we didn't sign anything."

a5848.speaker: Nigerian man deported from the US to Ghana (anonymous)
a5848.speech: Said the group is struggling in Togo without papers and relies on hotel staff to receive money from relatives abroad: "We're struggling to survive in Togo without any documentation." ; "None of us has family in Togo. We're just stuck in a hotel." ; "Right now, we're just trying to survive until our lawyers can help us with this situation." ; said the language barrier in Togo, where the official language is French, made it difficult to communicate.

a5848.speaker: Nigerian man deported from the US to Ghana (anonymous)
a5848.speech: Said that while in Ghana they had been asking for better living conditions because the military camp environment was "deplorable": "Life there was really hard, so we asked for a better place, better medication, better healthcare and better water."

a5848.speaker: Nigerian man deported from the US to Ghana (anonymous)
a5848.speech: Said his deportation had affected his family in the US: "I have a house in the US where my kids live. How am I supposed to pay the mortgage? I don't know how they'll manage while I'm gone. My kids can't see me, and it's just so stressful."

a5848.speaker: Nigerian man deported from the US to Ghana (anonymous)
a5848.speech: Said he was a member of the Yoruba Self-Determination Movement and feared that returning to Nigeria could lead to his arrest and torture because of his affiliation with the group; said he was under a US court-ordered protection that should have shielded him from deportation from the US.

a5848.speaker: Samuel Okudzeto Ablakwa, Ghana's Foreign Minister
a5848.speech: Previously said the government had accepted the deportees in the spirit of "pan-African empathy."

a5848.speaker: Samuel Okudzeto Ablakwa, Ghana's Foreign Minister
a5848.speech: Has since said Ghana received no financial reward for accepting the deportees.

a5848.speaker: Ghana's government
a5848.speech: The BBC has approached Ghana's government for comment (no comment reported) ; the government has said it plans to accept another 40 deportees.

a5848.speaker: Togolese authorities
a5848.speech: Have not commented on the alleged presence of the deportees on their territory.

a5848.speaker: John Mahama, President of Ghana
a5848.speech: Announced the deal for Ghana to take in nationals from various West African countries three weeks ago; said he had been approached by the US to accept the deportees and had agreed because there was free movement of people in West Africa.

a5848.speaker: Lawyers for the deportees
a5848.speech: Said the deportees had previously been held in a US detention facility before being flown out on a US military plane in shackles.

a5848.speaker: Lawyers for the deportees
a5848.speech: Have started legal action against both the US and Ghanaian governments, saying their clients' rights were violated.

a5848.speaker: Opposition MPs (Ghana)
a5848.speech: Have demanded an immediate suspension of the deportation agreement until it is ratified by parliament.

a5848.speaker: US government
a5848.speech: Has not given the reason for his deportation.

a5976.speaker: Mohamoud Moelim Abdulle, Commissioner of the Somali National Disaster Management Agency (SoDMA)
a5976.speech: Expressed his profound gratitude to the British government for its consistent support to the Somali people, specifically highlighting their assistance in emergency relief and in building the government's capacity to respond to disasters. He urged the British government to further increase its aid to help save the lives of those in dire need of humanitarian assistance.

a5976.speaker: Chris Pycroft, UK Director of Development Programmes (FCDO)
a5976.speech: Affirmed the UK's commitment to strengthening its partnership and increasing collaboration between SoDMA and other Somali government agencies. He stated that this increased cooperation is essential for ensuring that humanitarian responses are effective and lead to sustainable, long-term solutions for the challenges facing the nation.

a6057.speaker: United Nations High Commissioner for Human Rights
a6057.speech: According to the UN High Commissioner for Human Rights, nearly 3,000 people have been killed and another 2,880 injured since January 26 in ongoing attacks by the M23 armed group and its allies, with violence including the use of heavy weapons in populated areas.

a6057.speaker: Bintou Keita, UN Special Representative of the Secretary-General in the DRC and head of the peacekeeping mission (MONUSCO)
a6057.speech: “The situation is catastrophic,” said Bintou Keita. She described the ongoing humanitarian crisis in Goma, which is under M23 control, where dead bodies still lie in the streets. She also reported that youth are being forcibly recruited into the conflict, while human rights defenders, civil society actors, and journalists are increasingly targeted.

a6057.speaker: Bintou Keita, UN Special Representative of the Secretary-General in the DRC and head of the peacekeeping mission (MONUSCO)
a6057.speech: emphasized the urgency of humanitarian aid, particularly to Goma, where medical personnel are facing critical shortages, including power outages and a lack of fuel for essential services. She called on the international community to ensure that humanitarian assistance reaches those in need without delay.

a6057.speaker: Volker Türk, UN High Commissioner for Human Rights (UN rights chief)
a6057.speech: condemned the rise in sexual violence, noting that two hospitals in Goma were bombed on January 27, killing and injuring several patients, including women and children.

a6057.speaker: Patrick Muyaya Katembwe, DRC Minister of Communications and Media
a6057.speech: called out the continued military and financial support provided to armed groups by neighbouring Rwanda. He accused Rwanda of exacerbating the conflict in the region by supporting M23 forces for over three decades, largely due to the exploitation of DRC’s vast natural resources.

a6057.speaker: James Ngango, Rwanda’s Ambassador to the UN in Geneva
a6057.speech: denied the accusations, stating that the DRC-backed coalition was preparing for a large-scale attack on Rwanda. He alleged that weapons, including rockets and kamikaze drones, were being stockpiled near the border, posing a direct threat to Rwanda.

a6341.speaker: Laura Tomm-Bonde, IOM Chief of Mission
a6341.speech: “With these shelter kits (blankets, kitchen sets, sleeping mats, tarpaulins, ropes and carry-on bags) we hope to reduce the impact suffered by civilians in Palma. With this temporary access, IOM's Teams have been able to carry out an initial assessment on the current needs of IDPs in these hitherto inaccessible areas.”

a6341.speaker: Antonella D'Aprile, WFP Representative
a6341.speech: “It was an incredible joint humanitarian effort from the UN sister agencies, WFP, UNICEF and IOM in close coordination with the Government of Mozambique.”

a6341.speaker: International Organization for Migration (IOM)
a6341.speech: According to IOM, since 2017 more than 730 thousand people have been displaced due to conflict in Cabo Delgado.

a6341.speaker: Maria-Luisa Fornara, UNICEF Representative
a6341.speech: “In this situation of conflict and displacement the most vulnerable need our support most and these are women and children” ; “The emergency kits will prevent life-threatening diseases, improve the nutrition status of children and generally allow for a more dignified and safe living.”

a6341.speaker: UN agencies (IOM, UNICEF, WFP)
a6341.speech: UN agencies remain committed to providing rapid response to those who are most vulnerable in collaboration with partners and appeal to the donor community for continued support.

a6341.speaker: WFP Mozambique (@wfp_mozambique, Twitter post)
a6341.speech: “It was the first time UN agencies reached people in Palma with aid since late March. There are other organizations working in the ground, such as the Government of Mozambique, ONGs and Mozambican civil society organizations and networks.”

a6341.speaker: IOM Mozambique (@IOM_Mozambique, Twitter post)
a6341.speech: “Providing life-saving humanitarian survival kits to those in need are ongoing and of importance in #Mozambique. Access and security to hard-to-reach areas continues to be a challenge for humanitarian actors across #CaboDelgado province.”

a6341.speaker: UNICEF Moçambique (@UNICEF_Moz, Twitter post)
a6341.speech: Posted that the coordinated response by IOM Mozambique, WFP Mozambique and UNICEF offers relief to isolated people who had received no humanitarian aid from the UN in Mozambique since the armed attacks in Palma, Cabo Delgado, began at the end of March this year.

a6399.speaker: Dr. Shadrack Kamenya, Director of Conservation Science, Jane Goodall Institute (JGI) Tanzania
a6399.speech: Explains that farmers previously cleared riverine forests for short-term farming, causing a loss of soil fertility which led to the cutting of still more trees for farming ; “Smallholder farmers cleared riverine forests in order to produce crops but after a period of three years the soil fertility was lost, thus forcing them to clear other new forest areas in order to produce crops.”

a6399.speaker: JGI research/studies
a6399.speech: JGI's research shows that so far the use of compost manure in the project villages has had good results, with compost retaining water even in times of drought in fields that had lost fertility, thus enabling farmers to harvest between 100 and 200 percent more than they harvested before applying compost.

a6399.speaker: Dr. Shadrack Kamenya, Director of Conservation Science, Jane Goodall Institute (JGI) Tanzania
a6399.speech: Adds: “Village tree nursery operators have been setting business targets for the seedlings they raise, under supervision from JGI and district council experts.”

a6399.speaker: JGI Tanzania conservationists
a6399.speech: Advise villagers not only to plant and care for new tree seedlings, but also to leave the stumps of cut miombo trees to coppice so that the natural forest grows back again.

a6399.speaker: Reproductive health, family planning and gender equality experts from the district councils in the project area
a6399.speech: Advise villagers to have family sizes they can support and to abandon the misconceptions that prevent women and young people from properly contributing to the natural resource conservation agenda in their villages.

a6399.speaker: Robert Mkosamali, Communications and Storytelling specialist, Jane Goodall Institute Tanzania
a6399.speech: Notes that: “Research shows that the project and the climate change adaptation measures have reduced the destruction of chimpanzee habitat, with deforestation in riverine areas falling by 60 percent.”

a6399.speaker: Dr. Shadrack Kamenya, Director of Conservation Science, Jane Goodall Institute (JGI) Tanzania
a6399.speech: “When a chimpanzee dies, it is difficult to get a replacement, because only one infant is born in a period of four to five years, and very few chimpanzees give birth to twins,” explains Dr. Kamenya.

a6399.speaker: Dr. Shadrack Kamenya, Director of Conservation Science, Jane Goodall Institute (JGI) Tanzania
a6399.speech: “We are in the process of looking for an agricultural partner in order to obtain climate-smart technologies for women, with the aim of increasing production in rural agricultural zones, enabling market linkages and connecting farmers with commercial banks in order to access microloans.”

a6399.speaker: Aristides Kashula, Senior Forestry Officer, Jane Goodall Institute (JGI)
a6399.speech: “This framework allows district councils and village governments to obtain revenue for measurable and verifiable forest protection activities supervised by Carbon Tanzania.”

a6399.speaker: Bruno Mwaisaka, Natural Resources Officer, Tanganyika District Council
a6399.speech: “We conducted joint forest patrols every quarter, with JGI paying the costs of vehicles, fuel and allowances.”

a6399.speaker: Arfonsina Tambo, Village Executive Officer of Sigunga village
a6399.speech: “We have collaborated with JGI to provide education to villagers on reproductive health, organic farming, good governance, rights and equality, and the rule of law.”

a6399.speaker: Arfonsina Tambo, Village Executive Officer of Sigunga village
a6399.speech: “Compost manure has greatly increased maize harvests, thus reducing women's dependence on the lake.”

a6399.speaker: Neema Elias, leader of the COCOBA group in the Katumba area of Katavi region
a6399.speech: “The groups will continue to collect wild mushrooms in order to meet customers' demand.”

a6399.speaker: Athumani Makana, beekeeper
a6399.speech: “Beekeeping pays and changes lives,” says Makana, who now has a house, a motorcycle and milling machines, and plans to buy a car and to build rental houses.

a6399.speaker: Jason Ko, Senior Environment Advisor, USAID/Tanzania
a6399.speech: On the aim of the USAID-JGI partnership: “To protect wildlife and empower people. In 2018, we began the five-year USAID Western Tanzania Environmental Conservation project worth 20 million dollars. It has helped protect the chimpanzee population and their habitat and has empowered local communities. In 2023, the United States launched a 30-million-dollar programme with JGI/Tanzania, USAID Hope Through Action.”

a6399.speaker: Robin Holzhauer, Deputy Development and Communications Advisor, USAID/Tanzania
a6399.speech: “I want to explain that this is a long-term commitment. USAID began an environmental resource management programme in the 1990s, at the same time that Jane Goodall saw the pace of deforestation at Gombe. I mean, this happened before Fei Toto was even born. A long time. In 2003, we partnered and introduced sustainable community farming methods. Then we expanded the scope. We taught children ecological methods. We increased the amount of land under conservation through community-led land-use planning. We restored chimpanzee habitat.”

a6399.speaker: Jason Ko, Senior Environment Advisor, USAID/Tanzania
a6399.speech: On why the partnership works with villages rather than only the Gombe Reserve: “Chimpanzees live in forests outside Gombe. We work with the communities living near those areas, so that they can protect wildlife while benefiting from the nature that is there.”

a6399.speaker: Robin Holzhauer, Deputy Development and Communications Advisor, USAID/Tanzania
a6399.speech: “In addition, the communities near Gombe obtain income from conservation efforts. As our USAID Mission Director, Craig Hart, says, locally led governance is the core of this partnership.”

a6399.speaker: Craig Hart, USAID Mission Director (quoted by Robin Holzhauer)
a6399.speech: Says that locally led governance is the core of this partnership.

a6399.speaker: Robin Holzhauer, Deputy Development and Communications Advisor, USAID/Tanzania
a6399.speech: On the achievement they are most proud of: “How we benefit people and the environment and show people how they benefit from a healthy ecosystem. Some figures: nearly 253,000 people improved their incomes. Two village land forest reserves now exist, and 74 villages made and implemented land-use plans. We reached young people by starting 244 school environmental clubs.”

a6399.speaker: Jason Ko, Senior Environment Advisor, USAID/Tanzania
a6399.speech: “And data collected by JGI shows that USAID's investment helped reduce the rate of deforestation by 55 to 60 percent.”

a6399.speaker: Jason Ko, Senior Environment Advisor, USAID/Tanzania
a6399.speech: On the role of village authorities: “Village authorities are important. Outside the nationally managed Gombe National Park, the districts and villages manage the land. Villages make land-use plans in collaboration with district and national authorities to ensure that coordination is followed.”

a6399.speaker: Robin Holzhauer, Deputy Development and Communications Advisor, USAID/Tanzania
a6399.speech: “USAID also funded JGI's Tanzania branch directly, demonstrating a commitment to locally led development.”

a6399.speaker: Jason Ko, Senior Environment Advisor, USAID/Tanzania
a6399.speech: On what is new in Hope through Action: “The project includes matters concerning gender, agriculture and climate change. The project also supports efforts to collect and make good use of data.”

a6399.speaker: Robin Holzhauer, Deputy Development and Communications Advisor, USAID/Tanzania
a6399.speech: On the gender lens: “Women face obstacles to participating in decision-making. By supporting inclusive decision-making, women have a greater place and equal hope in making decisions. Achieving equality is important for Tanzania's sustainable development.”

a6399.speaker: Jason Ko, Senior Environment Advisor, USAID/Tanzania
a6399.speech: On the gender lens: “By including women and young people in decision-making processes, leaders address groups' problems through ideas that improve the economic condition of the whole community. When women cannot participate, we leave behind the expertise of 50 percent of the people.”

a6399.speaker: Jason Ko, Senior Environment Advisor, USAID/Tanzania
a6399.speech: On extending the approach to other ecosystems: “JGI introduced the community-based conservation approach in Tanzania with its Reforestation and Education programme in the Lake Tanganyika areas. USAID Tanzania's conservation programmes include community decision-making as a core concept.”

a6399.speaker: Robin Holzhauer, Deputy Development and Communications Advisor, USAID/Tanzania
a6399.speech: “For example, the USAID Heshimu Bahari project strengthens community-led management of important fish habitats, and the USAID Community Good Governance Project builds community capacity to be accountable to community and environmental needs. Americans and Tanzanians participate in programmes in their communities. USAID promotes local contribution in Tanzania.”

a6417.speaker: Joe Biden, US President
a6417.speech: Said at least 118 people have lost their lives and 600 people remain missing, and warned that the number of victims could still rise seriously ; For Joe Biden, "there is no doubt" that this devastation is due to climate change, which by warming sea waters makes the rapid intensification of storms more likely and increases the risk of more powerful hurricanes.

a6417.speaker: Joe Biden, US President
a6417.speech: Retorted to Donald Trump: "He is lying." "What irritates me (is that he) implies that we are not doing everything possible (...) It is false and it is irresponsible."

a6417.speaker: US media
a6417.speech: This is one of the most devastating hurricanes of recent decades, according to the US media.

a6417.speaker: Scientists
a6417.speech: According to scientists, the warming of sea waters makes the rapid intensification of storms more likely and increases the risk of more powerful hurricanes.

a6417.speaker: Donald Trump, Republican presidential candidate and former US President
a6417.speech: Promised to "bring plenty of humanitarian aid supplies, including fuel, equipment and water" to those in need ; "The federal government is not responding," he criticised, after previously accusing the government and the Democratic authorities of North Carolina of "deliberately not helping people in Republican areas."

a6417.speaker: Donald Trump, Republican presidential candidate and former US President
a6417.speech: Attacked his Democratic rival Kamala Harris directly, accusing her of being "on the move, campaigning" before stating that this was not the time to "talk politics."

a6417.speaker: Donald Trump, Republican presidential candidate and former US President
a6417.speech: Announced that he had asked Elon Musk, the head of SpaceX and close to the Republican, to deploy his Starlink satellite internet service in the region.

a6417.speaker: Kamala Harris, US Vice-President
a6417.speech: Cancelled campaign events to hold a meeting on Monday about the disaster and announced that she would be going to the field soon.

a6417.speaker: poweroutage.us (website monitoring the US electricity grid)
a6417.speech: More than 1.7 million homes and businesses were still without electricity on Monday afternoon, according to the site.

a6567.speaker: John Dramani Mahama, President of Ghana
a6567.speech: Announced during his televised address on Wednesday, May 7, 2025 on the successes chalked by his government within 120 days in office that Deloitte & Touche, an international audit and financial consultancy firm, is conducting an independent audit of the National Cathedral Project and is expected to present its final report to him by the end of the month ; highlighted a number of policy interventions rolled out by the Government over the period.

a6567.speaker: John Dramani Mahama, President of Ghana
a6567.speech: Indicated that the Minister of Finance had launched an inquiry into the collapse of indigenous banks and financial institutions ; stated that the Ministry of Energy and Green Transition is also investigating the PDS scandal.

a6567.speaker: US Government
a6567.speech: Halted the transfer of the funds, stating that private sector participation was a central reform under MCC's Ghana Power Compact.

a6567.speaker: John Dramani Mahama, President of Ghana
a6567.speech: Assured of his government's determination to unravel culprits involved in corrupt dealings and prosecute them in accordance with the laws of the country ; stated that a number of officials had been invited and questioned regarding their roles in the 13th All African Games ; added that the Attorney-General had led 11 charges against a former National Signals Bureau Director-General and others for various offences ; announced that charges would soon be led on the Accra SkyTrain and the National Service Scheme ghost names scandals as part of the government's anticorruption crusade on looting of state resources.

a6567.speaker: John Dramani Mahama, President of Ghana
a6567.speech: Expressed commitment to ensuring that his appointees served with integrity, accountability and transparency, hence the unveiling of the Code of Conduct to ensure the highest ethical standard.

a6575.speaker: Mohamed Ali, Head of Trade and Commercial Attaché, Embassy of the Federal Republic of Somalia
a6575.speech: Speaking at the recently held Embassies Business Fair and Conference, emphasized the pivotal role of Somalia and South Africa in unlocking new horizons in trade and economic diplomacy ; reaffirmed the Embassy's commitment to advancing economic diplomacy as a cornerstone of bilateral engagement, highlighting that trade and investment are no longer optional add-ons in diplomacy - they are the new currency of international relations ; said "Somalia and South Africa are shaping a new era of trade diplomacy. We are opening pathways for commerce in agriculture, fisheries, mining, and infrastructure. Together, we are unlocking Africa's economic future."

a6718.speaker: European Commission / EU executive (statement)
a6718.speech: Announced that all 27 EU member states assented to the retaliatory tariff measures on Wednesday, according to Politico ; “The EU considers U.S. tariffs unjustified and damaging, causing economic harm to both sides, as well as the global economy. The EU has stated its clear preference to find negotiated outcomes with the U.S., which would be balanced and mutually beneficial.”

a6718.speaker: Four EU diplomats with direct knowledge of the vote (anonymous)
a6718.speech: Said that only Hungary opposed the package, while the other 26 countries voted in favour.

a6718.speaker: Péter Szijjártó, Hungary's Foreign and Trade Minister
a6718.speech: Said in a post on X: “Today Hungary is voting against the @EU_Commission’s proposal to impose counter-tariffs on the US. Escalation is not the answer. Such measures would cause further damage to European economy and citizens by raising prices. The only way forward is negotiations, not retaliation.”

a6718.speaker: Péter Szijjártó, Hungary's Foreign and Trade Minister
a6718.speech: Said in another post: “Brussels and some European politicians are behaving irresponsibly towards the Western Balkans. Threats & contempt for elected leaders are very dangerous. Hungary has a responsible neighbourhood policy based on mutual respect.”

a6718.speaker: China’s Customs Department (statement obtained by SaharaReporters)
a6718.speech: “On April 8, 2025, the US government announced that it would increase the ‘reciprocal tariff’ on Chinese goods exported to the US from 34% to 84%. The US’s practice of escalating tariffs on China is a mistake on top of a mistake, which seriously infringes on China’s legitimate rights and interests and seriously damages the rules-based multilateral trading system. In accordance with the Tariff Law of the People’s Republic of China, the Customs Law of the People’s Republic of China, the Foreign Trade Law of the People’s Republic of China, and other laws and regulations and the basic principles of international law, and with the approval of the State Council, starting at 12:01 a.m. on April 10, 2025, the tariff increase measures on imported goods originating from the United States will be adjusted.”

a6718.speaker: Chinese authorities
a6718.speech: Announced an increase in tariffs on goods imported from the United States to 84%, and China vowed to “fight to the end” against what it called aggressive U.S. trade practices.

a7396.speaker: UNICEF (report)
a7396.speech: Said Wednesday that an estimated 680,000 children have been displaced by gang violence in Haiti, nearly double the number from a year ago, calling on the international community to step up help for the crisis-wracked Caribbean nation: “The number of children displaced by violence has almost doubled over the past year to approximately 680,000”; it added that more than 3.3 million children need humanitarian assistance, in what amounts to “a daily struggle for survival” ; “For countless children, trauma is a daily reality, and unless protection services are urgently restored, an entire generation risks growing up not only in fear but also under relentless exposure to violence and exploitation.”

a7396.speaker: Roberto Benes, UNICEF regional director for Latin America and the Caribbean
a7396.speech: “One of our messages is that Haiti is at a breaking point, we need to make clear this generation cannot keep waiting for help to come,” told AFP in an interview from Haiti.

a7396.speaker: United Nations (verification data)
a7396.speech: In 2024, the UN verified over 2,269 “grave violations” against 1,373 children, including 213 who were killed, 138 injured, 566 victims of sexual violence (including 406 rapes and 160 gang rapes), and 302 who were recruited by gangs.

a7396.speaker: UNICEF (estimates)
a7396.speech: Estimates that 2.7 million people, including 1.6 million women and children, now live in gang-controlled areas, nearly a quarter of the population.

a7421.speaker: Dr Ahmed Robleh Abdilleh, Minister of Health of Djibouti
a7421.speech: In his impassioned advocacy, stressed the importance of this unprecedented strategy, whose success rests on the involvement and commitment of all partners to contribute to its implementation and to achieving the set objectives in an optimal way ; also set out the main axes of the strategy, which give communities the pivotal and central role in this quest for social well-being by involving them more at all levels of the health pyramid.

a7421.speaker: UNICEF and the GAVI Alliance
a7421.speech: Have already confirmed their support for and commitment to the new national community health strategy.

a7421.speaker: Various participants at the round table
a7421.speech: Spoke to welcome the inclusive spirit of this strategy “by the community and for the community” on the path to better access to quality health care and services.

a7421.speaker: Ministry of Health of Djibouti
a7421.speech: Cited as the source of the report (“Source: Ministry of Health”); through this national community health strategy the health department aims to equip the country with a high-performing and resilient health system to fight effectively against the various diseases and thus reduce morbidity and mortality among the population, particularly the most vulnerable, namely maternal and child health.
